summaries.summary: I compared holtburger's chargen code with retail and OpenAC. On the holtburger side that was holtburger-core CharacterGenBuilder, the holtburger-content catalog, the protocol pack/unpack, the plugins/character-creation.js wizard and the wasm sendCharGenResult/catalog exports. On the retail side it was the decomp (CharGenState, ACCharGenData, gmCGSkillsPage, gmCharGenMainUI, ACCharGenResult::CG_Pack/CG_UnPack and VerifyCharacterGenerationResult) plus OpenAC's CharGen/RuntimeCharacterCreationState. I also read the real CharGen record (0x0E000002) out of ~/ac_base_dats/client_portal.dat with a read-only script, and the baked data/skill-table.json. In the real data every heritage has 330 attribute and 52 skill credits, the only heritage skill override is Arcane Lore (0, 2), and all six preset templates cost exactly 52 under retail rules. The 0xF656 field order, the string alignment and the 0xF643 parse match retail, except that the trailing checksum is missing. The rule layer has two HIGH bugs that make the wizard broken against real data. First, specialising is charged trained + specialised (War Magic 44 instead of 28), so every preset template is over budget and the default flow cannot pass the Skills page. Second, every non-template skill is sent as Inactive, so the free skills (Run, Jump, Magic Defense, Loyalty, Salvaging, Arcane Lore) are never trained; a retail server would reject the packet. Smaller issues: clothing colours go out as list indices where retail sends palette-template keys; the retail name formatter is not applied; and unspent attribute credits are refused although retail allows them after a warning. One LOW item is not in the list below: 0xF643 rejections are shown as raw enum names. Retail maps them to ID_Character_Err_* text (likely 'The name you have selected is already in use.', 'Sorry, but that name is not permitted. Please choose another.', 'You do not have the privileges to make an administrator character.', and otherwise 'The server cannot create your new character at this time. Please try again later.'). An unknown code also makes the unpack fail, which leaves the wizard stuck in Submitting.

I compared holtburger's external-container window with the retail decomp and with OpenAC. On the holtburger side that is plugins/corpse-loot-bar.js, which container-panel.js routes every kind=21 to, the wasm ViewContents/CloseGroundContainer/groundContainerId code, item_drag/inventory_helpers drops and the picking.js use path. On the retail side it is gmExternalContainerUI, ClientUISystem::SetGroundObject/OnViewContents, ItemHolder::AttemptSetGroundObject/AttemptPlaceIn3D and CPlayerSystem::UsingItem plus the object-range handler. On the OpenAC side it is ExternalContainerState, ExternalContainerController and the lifecycle controller, plus their tests. Holtburger already has retail's one-window model and the shipped use-3/death-5/items-2 pieces. The gaps are in when the window opens and closes. (1) Every ViewContents opens or replaces the window, including the sub-packs ACE sends right after a chest/corpse opens and the player's own packs (pickup, vendor purchase, quest reward). The 1 s despawn poll then closes it, so any container holding a pack can't be looted. Retail opens only the requested ground object. (2) There is no client range exit, teleport/death close or vendor exclusivity. The window lingers up to ACE's 5 s heartbeat, or until the ~25 s prune after a portal, and a Take in that time walks the player back. (3) A 3D drop onto a container that isn't open drops the item on the ground; retail refuses it. (4) A locked chest gives no text. (5) Packs inside a chest can't be browsed. Not findings: holtburger closing with NoLongerViewingContents where retail/OpenAC send a toggle Use is the safer choice with ACE, because a Use that lands after ACE's own close re-opens the chest and walks the player back (Player_Use.cs:197). The blanket corpse drop refusal matches ACE ('container is Corpse' is refused, Player_Inventory.cs:853-857).

I compared holtburger-web's vendor BUY path against OpenAC and the retail decomp, and checked server behaviour against ACE's Vendor.cs and Player_Commerce.cs. The holtburger side covered vendor-ui.js, commerce_logic.js, the wasm VendorInfo cache (game_event.rs and lib.rs VendorStateJs), the 0xA0 arm and BuyActionData. The OpenAC side covered VendorUiController, VendorStagingList, VendorApproach, VendorRequests, VendorShopItemMaterializer, VendorSplitPolicy and their tests. The decomp side covered gmVendorUI::BuySingleItem, HandleButtonClicks, OpenVendor, InqListSlotCount and AdoptAsContents; VendorItemsUI::UpdateItemsList, AddToBuyList, RemoveFromShop and OpenVendor; VendorBuyUI::UpdateTransactionValue; ItemProfile::UnPack; CM_Vendor::Event_Buy; and ACCWeenieObject::ServerSaysAttemptFailed. Several parts are already correct: the single-stack ShopSystem::SellPrice math, the direction of the two rates, the trade-note rate, the alt-currency balance and the 2026-10-07 range close.

The gaps are in the flow around the formula:
1. Nothing is refused before sending. Retail refuses with "You don't have enough money" or "You must empty some slots in your backpack first", and a refused Buy All currently loses the whole list.
2. ACE's purchase refusal is shown as "You can't wield that!" plus a "WeenieError 0x0000" toast.
3. A stock line is priced as one lump and is not limited by its supply or by retail's 5000 cap, because the wasm drops ItemProfile.amount and max_stack_size.
4. A same-vendor refresh leaves stale entries on the buying list.
5. The category filter mislabels four item-type bits.
6. The Buy message lacks retail's trailing AlternateCurrencyId, and every VendorInfo adds a non-retail line to the Trade chat category.

Not reported because they are lower value or large:
- The close button has no confirmation ("You have not completed all transactions. Are you sure you want to leave this vendor?", HandleButtonClicks case 0x100000D6).
- Retail's starting quantity is the full stack except for 0x0DC41CB0 types, and its cost texts are not copied.
- Handle_VendorInfo's SetGroundObject(0,1): in retail, opening a vendor closes an open corpse or chest.
- @fillcomps (gmVendorUI::FillComponentList) is missing.
- "You can't wield that!" is used for every code-0 0xA0 on items, where retail builds the text from the outstanding request type.

ACE never resells stackables (Vendor.cs:631), so ACE's unique stock is always single non-stackable items and no whole-stack overcharge exists today.

I compared holtburger-web's PK handling with the retail decomp, using OpenAC as the worked reference. On the holtburger side I read objectIsAttackable and its callers in picking.js, entities.js and target_cycle.js, the spell target pre-check, the examine header, the character panel, the world-use paths, the slash-command router and the WeenieError text table. On the retail side I read ObjectIsAttackable, ExecuteAttack/GetAttackTarget/AutoTarget, the PK-status bit update (stat 0x86), ObjectCompatibleWithSpellTargetType/CastSpell, ItemHolder::UseObject and the PK/NPK altar dialogs, HandleFailureEvent, DoPKLite/DoPKArena/DoPKLArena, CharExamineUI and gmStatManagementUI::UpdatePKStatus. Several things already match retail: the attack rule itself, the spell pre-check (it reads live flags and the pet owner; retail does no PK check on spells), radar and bracket PK colours, the player-vs-player collision pass-through, and the PK jump-stamina rule. The main bug is that the melee/missile attack gate, Tab and auto-target, combat-mode entry and target tracking all read PK bits saved when the object was created. After any mid-session PK change (altar, @pklite, PK death and respite), a player who has just become PK cannot attack other PKs until they relog. The same stale data has no pet owner, so pets count as attack targets. Smaller gaps: using a PK or NPK altar skips retail's confirmation dialog; @pklite/@pkl, @pkarena/@pka and @pklarena/@pla are missing, so a player cannot enter PK Lite at all; the PK status and PK refusal messages print as garbled fallbacks (for example "You are now p k lite.") or reworded text; and the examine and character panels never show "Player Killer Lite" or "Non-Player Killer".

findings.title: Specialized skill cost double-counts the trained cost (trained+specialized instead of the specialized total), so every retail profession template is over budget
findings.decomp_evidence: CharGenState::UpdateRemainingSkillCredits (acclient.c:495070) charges only ACCharGenData::GetSkillSpecializedCost for SAC 3 (:495086) and only GetSkillTrainedCost for SAC 2, never both. CharGenState::SetSkillLevel (:495350) refunds the old tier's full cost and charges the new tier's full cost. ACCharGenData::GetSkillSpecializedCost (:494279) returns the heritage SkillCG.primaryCost (:494304), otherwise SkillBase._specialized_cost (node+28, :494337; acclient.h:40229-40230 _trained_cost/_specialized_cost). gmCGSkillsPage::IncreaseSkillLevel (:189055) allows Trained->Specialized when `(iSpecCost - iTrainCost) <= remainingSkillCredits` (:189087), so the upgrade costs the difference. The server-side ACCharGenResult::VerifyCharacterGenerationResult (:498868) sums the same way and rejects `v31 > hg.numSkillCredits` (:499104). Real DAT: data/skill-table.json (0x0E000004) gives War Magic 16/28, Melee Defense 10/20, Life Magic 12/20, Missile Weapons 6/12. CharGen 0x0E000002 (parsed this session): 52 skill credits per heritage. All six templates sum to exactly 52 under the retail rule: Bow Hunter 8+2+12+8+2+20, Swashbuckler 8+6+2+20+12+4, Life Caster 16+8+6+2+20, War Mage 12+12+28, Wayfarer 36+16, Soldier 12+40. ACE agrees: PlayerFactory.cs:184-202 trains for TrainedCost and then specialises for UpgradeCostFromTrainedToSpecialized (= SpecializedCost - TrainedCost, ACE.DatLoader SkillBase.cs:31).

The costs are taken unchanged from SkillBase._specialized_cost / SkillCG.primary_cost (crates/holtburger-content/src/character_gen.rs:50-51, 191-192). tests/character_creation.test.cjs:221-225 pins 'Axe spec = 6 + 4'. The CLI has the same bug (apps/holtburger-cli/src/pages/selection/creation.rs:742). The skills page gates Next on this budget (character-creation.js:1372-1373).
findings.discrepancy: For a specialised skill holtburger charges trained + specialized, but specialized_cost is already the total. War Magic costs 44 instead of 28. With the real DAT every preset template goes over the 52-credit budget: Bow Hunter 72, Swashbuckler 70, Life Caster 64, War Mage 74, Wayfarer 60, Soldier 72. The default wizard flow (pickDefaultTemplate picks Bow Hunter) reaches a Skills page with Next disabled ('Skill budget exceeded'), and the Rust validator emits SkillBudgetExceeded for builds that are legal in retail. Only Arcane Lore comes out right, because its heritage normal cost is 0.
findings.proposed_change: (1) In character_gen.rs validate_skills, use `Specialized => spent_credits += i64::from(costs.specialized_cost)`, and document CharacterGenSkillCosts.specialized_cost as the TOTAL cost to specialise (SkillBase._specialized_cost / SkillCG.primaryCost). (2) In character-creation.js computeSkillBudget, use class 3 -> `c.specializedCost`, and set the cost cell at :1349 to `c.specializedCost`. Optionally label the upgrade step as retail does: specializedCost - trainedCost. Fix the JSDoc at :162-168. (3) In the CLI, change creation.rs advancement_cost (:742) to Specialized => specialized_cost; skill_delta_cost then gives retail's (spec - train) step automatically. (4) In src/lib.rs, fix the doc example near get_character_gen_catalog: 'trainedCost: 6, specializedCost: 4' should show spec >= train.

Add a real-data case: load data/skill-table.json costs plus the Arcane Lore override {14: trained 0, spec 2}, and assert that each of the six DAT templates sums to exactly 52 and is valid against budget 52. findings.title: Non-template skills are sent as Inactive and the free skills are never trained (retail ResetSkillLevels/bUntrainable not ported)
findings.decomp_evidence: CharGenState::ResetSkillLevels (acclient.c:495832) sets every SkillTable skill with valid costs to Untrained (=1, :495887). It sets Trained (=2, :495883) when the heritage-adjusted trained cost is <= 0, and Specialized when both costs are <= 0. CharGenState::ApplyTemplate (:496607) calls ResetSkillLevels and then applies the template's normal/primary skills through SetSkillLevel when affordable. gmCGSkillsPage::DoSkillRecords (:189729) sets `bUntrainable = iTrainCost != 0` and `bUnspecializable = iSpecCost != 0`. A heritage SkillCG with normalCost 0 forces iTrainCost = 0 and bUntrainable = 0 (:189984-189988). DecreaseSkillLevel (:189101) refuses to lower a skill whose flag is false. The server-side VerifyCharacterGenerationResult fails unless the number of non-Inactive classes equals the SkillTable entry count: `if ( v28 != *(_DWORD *)(v26 + 72) )` (:499087), where +72 is PackableHashTable._currNum (acclient.h:40184-40195). Real DAT: 38 SkillTable skills. Trained cost is 0 for Magic Defense 15, Jump 22, Run 24, Loyalty 36 and Salvaging 40, and every heritage has SkillCG (14 Arcane Lore, 0, 2).
findings.openac_evidence: src/AcDream.Runtime/Session/RuntimeCharacterCreationState.cs:484-500 ResetSkillLevelsLocked (`trainedCost > 0 ? Untrained : specializedCost <= 0 ? Specialized : Trained`) and :419-444 ApplyTemplateLocked (reset, then template Trained/Specialized with the affordability check). As a result all 55 wire slots carry retail classes.
findings.holt_evidence: plugins/character-creation.js:330-339 seedSkillStatesFromTemplate seeds only the template's skills. buildCharGenPayload :293 uses `new Array(expectedSkillSlots).fill(0)`, so every other skill is sent as 0 (Inactive). The skills page (:1332) offers Untrained/Trained/Specialized for every skill: free skills can be untrained, and an unset skill displays 'Untrained' while being sent as 0. The Rust validator accepts this (crates/holtburger-core/src/character_gen.rs:369 `if *advancement == SkillAdvancementClass::Inactive { continue; }`). In contrast, the createTestCharacter path (src/lib.rs:42423-42433) fills every catalog skill with minimum_skill_advancement_for_heritage. ACE: PlayerFactory.cs:173 `if (sac == SkillAdvancementClass.Inactive) continue;` and Creature_Skills.cs GetCreatureSkill later creates the missing skill as Untrained.
findings.discrepancy: A wizard-made Bow Hunter goes out with 6 non-Inactive classes where retail sends 38. A retail server rejects that as corrupt. On ACE the character silently ends up with Run, Jump, Magic Defense, Loyalty and Salvaging untrained (plus Arcane Lore when the template does not train it). It also misses the +5 creation ranks that TrainSkill(…, applyCreationBonusXP) grants (Player_Skills.cs:182-186). The UI also lets the user untrain free skills, which retail forbids.
findings.proposed_change: (1) Add an exported pure `resetSkillStates(catalogSkills, costsForSkill)` to character-creation.js that ports ResetSkillLevels: for each catalog.skills entry take c = costsForSkill(id), then class = c.trainedCost <= 0 ? (c.specializedCost <= 0 ? 3 : 2) : 1. (2) Make seeding reset-then-template: normal skills -> 2 and primary -> 3, skipping any step that is not affordable, as ApplyTemplate does. Call it from applyHeritageDefaults and the heritage/gender/template change handlers. (3) In renderSkillsPage, disable the Untrained option when c.trainedCost === 0 (bUntrainable) and the Trained option for a Specialized skill whose specializedCost === 0 (bUnspecializable). (4) Rust validate_skills: add an error when any skill in catalog.skill_definitions is Inactive (the retail count rule) or below its cost floor (trained_cost <= 0 requires >= Trained). Base minimum_skill_advancement_for_template on costs only, because retail has no template-list floors and the DAT has no 'Custom' template.
findings.test_plan: `node tests/character_creation.test.cjs`. New cases: (a) resetSkillStates over data/skill-table.json with override {14: {0, 2}} gives class 2 for 14, 15, 22, 24, 36 and 40, and class 1 for the other 32 skills. (b) Reset plus Bow Hunter, then buildCharGenPayload with expectedSkillSlots 55, gives exactly 38 non-zero entries and 0 for every slot not in the table. (c) Untrain is refused for Run. Rust, in crates/holtburger-core/src/character_gen.rs mod tests: validate_rejects_inactive_table_skill and validate_rejects_untrained_free_skill (orchestrator runs cargo). The JS part needs no rebuild; the Rust validator part does.

verify.reasons: Decomp, re-read: the CharGenState ctor (acclient.c ~497960) sets totalNumSkills = max SkillTable key + 1 (55) and zero-fills skillLevels. ResetSkillLevels (:495832) walks ids 1..totalNumSkills-1. For ids present in the SkillTable hash with costs >= 0 it sets 3 when trained<=0 and spec<=0, 2 when trained<=0, and 1 otherwise. Ids not in the table stay 0. ApplyTemplate (:496607) resets, then applies normal skills via SetSkillLevel(Trained) and primary skills via an inline spec charge, only when affordable. DoSkillRecords sets bUntrainable = iTrainCost != 0 and bUnspecializable = iSpecCost != 0 (:189963-189967). A heritage normalCost of 0 zeroes the trained cost and clears bUntrainable (:189985-189987). DecreaseSkillLevel (:189101) honours those flags. VerifyCharacterGenerationResult counts the non-zero classes and fails when the count differs from *(v26+72) (:499087). +72 is SkillTable._skillBaseHash._currNum: the hash starts at +56, as the ctor's begin(v2+56) and GetSkillTrainedCost's +64/+68 confirm. In the real DAT that count is 38. Holtburger: seedSkillStatesFromTemplate (:330) seeds only template skills. buildCharGenPayload (:293) fills the rest with 0. The select at :1332 has no flag gating. validate_skills skips Inactive (:369). ACE PlayerFactory.cs:173 skips Inactive. Player_Skills.AlwaysTrained (ArcaneLore, Jump, Loyalty, MagicDefense, Run, Salvaging) is only used for untrain/reset, so nothing auto-trains at creation. A retail client's Trained-Run packet succeeds on ACE (TrainSkill fails if the skill is already >= Trained), so the human weenie cannot pre-train Run. Holtburger characters therefore end up with those skills untrained, without the +5 ranks / 526 XP (Player_Skills.cs:182-186). OpenAC ResetSkillLevelsLocked :484-500 and ApplyTemplateLocked :419-444 were verified. Not tracked anywhere.
verify.corrections: The proposed fix is UNSAFE as written. holtburger-dat injects 10 retired skills into the SkillTable hash (skill_table.rs:91-121: Axe 1, Bow 2, Crossbow 3, Dagger 4, Mace 5, Spear 9, Staff 10, Sword 11, Thrown 12, Unarmed 13) with trained 0, spec 0 and chargen_use 1 (:112). They reach CharacterGenCatalog.skill_definitions, the getCharacterGenCatalog 'skills' array and costsForSkill (0/0). A naive resetSkillStates over catalog.skills would mark all 10 Specialized (both costs <= 0 gives class 3). That makes 48 non-zero classes, which a retail server rejects because the count must be 38. ACE, which also injects them with 0 costs (DatManager AddRetiredSkills), would grant free specialized retired weapon skills. The proposed Rust rule 'error when any skill in catalog.skill_definitions is Inactive' has the same problem: it would force the retired slots non-Inactive. A related pre-existing bug: the wizard already lists these 10 retired skills, because renderSkillsPage filters only on chargenUse (:1323), and the user can Specialize them for 0 credits. createTestCharacter (lib.rs:42423-42433) and the CLI reset (creation.rs:675-685) already send them as Trained.
verify.implementation_notes: MANDATORY: range every chargen rule over real DAT SkillTable entries only. Option A: add an explicit marker, e.g. a 'retired' bool on holtburger-dat SkillBase (binrw calc/default false, true for the injected entries), carried to CharacterGenSkillDefinition and exported in getCharacterGenCatalog JSON. Then update the SkillBase struct literals in holtburger-world/src/player/tests.rs:1798 and holtburger-cli .../character/render.rs:706. Option B: a non-breaking SkillBase::is_retired_placeholder() keyed on the injected 'Retired skill:' description, icon 0 and 0/0 costs. JS: export resetSkillStates(catalogSkills, costsForSkill). Skip retired entries and skillId 0, since retail loops start at 1. Skip costs < 0 or null. class = trained<=0 ? (spec<=0 ? 3 : 2) : 1. Then applyTemplateSkills(states, template, costsForSkill, budget): normal skills -> 2, then primary -> 3, each kept only if (remaining + refund of the current tier - new tier cost) >= 0. Use it at applyHeritageDefaults (:1516) and in the template-change handler (:906). Olthoi heritages 12/13 force template 0, as ApplyTemplate does. renderSkillsPage: skip retired skills. Disable Untrained when the heritage-adjusted trainedCost === 0. Disable lowering Specialized->Trained when specializedCost === 0. Optionally disable options the budget cannot afford. Rust validate_skills: for every non-retired skill_definition with id >= 1, Inactive is an error, and below the cost floor is an error (trained<=0 requires >=Trained; trained<=0 and spec<=0 require Specialized). Retired or absent slots must be Inactive. Update build_test_character_request (lib.rs:42423) and the CLI reset (creation.rs:675) to leave retired slots Inactive. Update the Rust fixtures: test_build's Inactive slots 3/4 become Untrained, and skill 0 is skipped. Tests: in tests/character_creation.test.cjs, (a) reset over data/skill-table.json with override {14:{0,2}} gives class 2 for 14, 15, 22, 24, 36 and 40, and class 1 for the other 32. (b) Reset plus Bow Hunter plus buildCharGenPayload(expectedSkillSlots 55) gives exactly 38 non-zero entries, all non-table slots 0, and 52 spent. (c) An injected retired entry {skillId:1, trainedCost:0, specializedCost:0, retired:true} stays 0. Update the [5] seedSkillStatesFromTemplate cases. findings.title: Character name rules differ from retail ACCharGenData::FormatName (digits allowed, hyphens rejected, 3-char minimum, no case normalisation)
findings.decomp_evidence: ACCharGenData::FormatName (acclient.c:488655): trims trailing spaces and caps the name at 32. It keeps only A-Z, a-z, apostrophe, hyphen and space; digits and other characters are dropped. It drops leading, doubled and trailing spaces. Apostrophes and hyphens must touch letters: no doubles, no leading apostrophe. Case is then normalised with CharCase (acclient.h:7735): the first letter is upper and the rest lower, except the letter after a space, hyphen or apostrophe, or after Mac/Mc/Fitz/Von/Van/De/Di/Du/Le/La, which stays as typed; I/V/X roman-numeral words become upper. CharGenState::SetName (:495399) applies it to every name of 32 characters or fewer (:495407). gmCharGenMainUI::DoFinish (:278604) trims "[] " from both ends (:278642) and refuses an empty name ('You must enter a name for this character!'). The server-side VerifyCharacterGenerationResult requires 1..32 characters and `strcmp(FormatName(name), name) == 0` (:499125).
findings.openac_evidence: src/AcDream.Runtime/Session/RuntimeCharacterCreationState.cs:1131-1136 TrySetName only truncates to 32. TryBeginFinish (:1161+) trims and refuses an empty name. There is no FormatName port, so OpenAC is only a partial reference; it does allow 1-character names.
findings.holt_evidence: plugins/character-creation.js:151-160 validateCharacterName: trim, `trimmed.length < 3` rejected (:154), at most 32, `/^[a-zA-Z0-9 ']+$/` (:156). It accepts digits, rejects hyphens, does no case normalisation, and lets doubled spaces and a leading apostrophe through. The Rust side only checks non-empty (crates/holtburger-core/src/character_gen.rs:247). ACE does no character or case check (CharacterHandler.cs CharacterCreateEx: taboo, creature-name and in-use checks only).
findings.discrepancy: On ACE, holtburger can create names retail never produces ('bob2', 'bOB', "'Bob  Smith"), and it blocks names retail allows ('Jean-Luc', 'Al', 'X'). A retail server rejects any name that is not already in FormatName form.
findings.proposed_change: Port FormatName as an exported pure `formatCharacterName(raw)` in character-creation.js, as a direct port of the retail state machine above. Run it when the name field loses focus and on submit, and write the formatted result back to the field as retail SetName does. Validate: trim "[] "; the formatted name is non-empty and at most 32 characters; formatted === submitted. Remove the 3-character minimum and the digit allowance. Optionally mirror it as holtburger_core::character_gen::format_name with a validator check; that part would need a wasm rebuild.

verify.reasons: ACCharGenData::FormatName (acclient.c:488655), traced by hand. Trailing spaces are trimmed and only the first min(len,32) chars are scanned. The filter keeps A-Z, a-z, apostrophe, space and hyphen; signed-char bytes >= 0x80 fail the letter test and are dropped. Neighbour tests use the PREVIOUS INPUT char and the next char. A space is dropped if prev is space or 0, or next is 0. A hyphen is kept only if prev is a letter and next is a letter or hyphen. An apostrophe is kept if prev is a letter, or if prev is non-zero, not an apostrophe, and next is a letter. Case pass (enum CharCase acclient.h:7735: 0 UPPER, 1 LOWER, 2 EITHER): cases[0]=UPPER and the rest LOWER. After a space, hyphen or apostrophe the next char is EITHER. Mac/Mc/Fitz/Von/Van/De/Di/Du/Le/La prefixes, matched case-insensitively, make the following char EITHER. A letter run made only of uppercase I/V/X becomes UPPER. All 9 proposed vectors match the trace: bob2->Bob, BOB SMITH->Bob Smith, bob smith->Bob smith, MACDONALD->MacDonald, jean-luc->Jean-luc, o''neil->O'neil, a--b->A-b, Bob III->Bob III, '  x '->X. SetName (:495399) applies FormatName when strlen <= 32. DoFinish trims '[] ' (:278642) and refuses an empty name. The server-side check needs 1..32 chars and strcmp(FormatName(name), name)==0 (:499125). The client_local_English.dat strings were checked ('You must enter a name for this character!' etc.). Holtburger validateCharacterName (:151-160) applies a 3-char minimum and /^[a-zA-Z0-9 ']+$/, which accepts digits and rejects hyphens. Rust only checks non-empty (core :247). OpenAC has no FormatName port. ACE has no charset check.
verify.corrections: Validating 'formatted === submitted' is circular, because the wizard submits the formatted name. The meaningful client check is the server's: FormatName(formatted) === formatted. Retail FormatName is not always idempotent ('a - b' gives 'A  b', and the second pass gives 'A b'), so check idempotence locally and refuse rather than get a Corrupt reply. Also update the name hint at :1004 ('3-32 characters; letters, numbers...') and the existing [2] test cases (rejects 'ab', accepts digits, rejects 'Foo-Bar'), which encode the old rules.
verify.implementation_notes: In plugins/character-creation.js, export formatCharacterName(raw) as a direct port. (1) Strip leading and trailing '[', ']' and ' ' (DoFinish). (2) Trim trailing spaces and take window = s.slice(0,32). (3) Filter, with prev = previous INPUT char (null at start, including dropped chars), next = window[i+1] or null, and letterish(c) = /[A-Za-z]/ or charCode >= 0x80. Keep letters. Keep a space unless prev is space or null, or next is null. Keep an apostrophe iff letterish(prev), or (prev not null, prev != apostrophe, letterish(next)). Keep a hyphen iff prev != hyphen, letterish(prev), and (letterish(next) or next == hyphen). Drop everything else, including digits and non-ASCII. (4) cases: cases[0]=UPPER, the rest LOWER. For each word start w (0, or i+1 after an output space, hyphen or apostrophe): if w > 0, cases[w]=EITHER. Then case-insensitive prefixes at w: Mac sets cases[w+3]; Mc sets cases[w+2]; Fitz sets cases[w+4]; Von/Van set cases[w+3]; De/Di/Du set cases[w+2]; Le/La set cases[w+2] (guard the index < length). (5) For each maximal letterish run whose chars are all uppercase 'I', 'V' or 'X', set cases to UPPER. (6) Apply LOWER to A-Z and UPPER to a-z; leave EITHER as typed. validateCharacterName(name): f = formatCharacterName(name); ok iff the raw trimmed length is <= 32, f.length is 1..32, and formatCharacterName(f) === f. Write f back to state.name and the input on blur and on submit. Drop the 3-char minimum. Tests: in tests/character_creation.test.cjs, the 9 vectors above, 'Al' and 'X' accepted, 33 chars rejected, '[Bob]' -> 'Bob', 'Dean' typed 'DEAN' -> 'DeAn' (prefix quirk), and 'a - b' refused as non-idempotent. Rewrite the [2] cases. JS only, no wasm rebuild. No URL flag (HUD rule).

Only non-container targets fall through to UIAttemptPutIn3D. IsContainer (:220515) = `(pwd._bitfield & 0x00800000) || _itemsCapacity || _containersCapacity`; the decompiler shows the mask as a string address, and :173725-173727 (`& 0xFF7FFFFF`) gives its value. groundObject is cleared by 0x52 (:394878-394880). Locked updates: ACCWeenieObject::OnStatUpdated stype 3 → SetOpenable(val == 0) (:437080-437084).
findings.openac_evidence: src/AcDream.Core/Items/ItemInteractionPolicy.cs:377-383 DecidePlacement: `if (target.IsContainer) { if ((target.Flags & Openable) == 0) Reject($"The {..} is locked"); if (target.Id != input.GroundObjectId) Reject($"You must open the {..} first"); PlaceInContainer }`.
findings.holt_evidence: plugins/inventory_helpers.js:615-636 decideItemDrop WORLD runs isSelf → isOpenContainer (move) → trade → creature give → `return { op: "drop", guid, amount };` (:635). There is no container branch, and executeItemAction 'drop' calls dropItem (item_drag.js:710-717). plugins/item_drag.js:495-523 describeWorldEntity sets `isOpenContainer: !!ground && ground === g` (:521) from wasm groundContainerId (lib.rs:37317-37324). game_event.rs:826 overwrites that on every ViewContents (sub-packs, own packs), and the ContainerClosed arm (session/messages/mod.rs:660-684) never clears it. ACE answers a drop into a closed landscape container with TheContainerIsClosed (external/ACE Player_Inventory.cs:951-957). tests/inventory_drag_rules.test.mjs:185-186 pins only 'no entity → drop'.
findings.discrepancy: Dragging a pack item onto a closed or locked chest, or an unopened corpse, sends DropItem and the item lands at the player's feet. Retail prints the refusal and sends nothing. While a chest holding a pack is open, a 3D drop onto that open chest also drops to the ground, because groundContainerId now names the sub-pack. After a chest closes, a 3D drop is still treated as 'open', sent, and refused by ACE.
findings.proposed_change: (1) In describeWorldEntity add `isContainer`: objectIntProperty(g,6) (ItemsCapacity) non-zero, or objectIntProperty(g,7) (ContainersCapacity) non-zero, or (odf & 0x00800000). Compute `isOpenContainer` from the UI: `window.__corpseLootBar?.isOpen?.() && window.__corpseLootBar.current?.() === g`, falling back to groundContainerId only if the plugin is absent. (2) decideItemDrop WORLD, after the creature give and before `drop`: `if (ent.isContainer) return reject(ent.openable ? `You must open the ${ent.name || "container"} first` : `The ${ent.name || "container"} is locked`);`. findings.test_plan: Extend tests/inventory_drag_rules.test.mjs next to 'world: no entity → drop' (:185), run with `node tests/inventory_drag_rules.test.mjs`. findings.decomp_evidence: gmVendorUI::BuySingleItem (acclient.c:244716). It prices the item with VendorProfile::VendorSellPrice(pwd, amount). For a pyreal vendor, `if ( v9 > v2->m_totalValue )` sends ECM_UI::SendNotice_DisplayStringInfo(0x1A, 'You don't have enough money') at :244764; for alt currency the test is `v9 > trade_num - m_last_sale` (:244783). It then checks room in the main pack. A container-class shop item (pwd._bitfield & 0x800000 BF_REQUIRES_PACKSLOT, or _itemsCapacity, or _containersCapacity) is refused when GetNumContainedContainers(player) == player._containersCapacity. Any other item is refused when GetNumContainedItems(player) == player._itemsCapacity, with 'You must empty some slots in your backpack first' (:244808). Only after both checks does it call CM_Vendor::Event_Buy. Buy All is gmVendorUI::HandleButtonClicks case 0x100000CA: the same money test on m_transactionValue (:247055 / :247066), then gmVendorUI::InqListSlotCount (:243174; a non-stackable line adds `amount` slots at :243195, a stackable line adds 1 at :243205) against capacity minus contents (:247075-247080). Only then does it call SendShopEvent and flush the list. m_totalValue is CoinValue (gmVendorUI::UpdateTotalValue :246499, InqInt 0x14). GetNumContainedItems and GetNumContainedContainers (:436428 / :436442) count only the player's own _itemsList / _containersList, i.e. the main pack.

findings.discrepancy: Retail refuses an unaffordable purchase, or one with no room, in the client with one of two fixed texts and keeps the buying list. Holtburger always sends. ACE then refuses with no text at all when the cause is money, and Buy All has already emptied the player's list.
findings.proposed_change:
Add two functions to commerce_logic.js:
- `vendorBuySlotsNeeded(lines)`, a port of InqListSlotCount. For each line, a maxStackSize of 1 or less adds `amount` slots, otherwise 1. A packSlot line counts toward containers.
- `vendorBuyRefusal({cost, balance, need, used, cap})`. It returns 'You don't have enough money' when cost > balance. Otherwise it returns 'You must empty some slots in your backpack first' when need.containers > cap.containers - used.containers or need.items > cap.items - used.items. Otherwise null. Money is tested first, as in retail.

The player-side numbers come from the existing inventory_helpers.packCapacity(rows, MAIN_PACK_KEY / PACKS_KEY, {mainCap: handle.playerItemsCapacity, packsCap: handle.playerContainersCapacity}). Use copyInventoryRow rows, because commerce_window.inventoryRows drops requiresBackpackSlot.
